assignments.value: Systems Programming & Low-Level Architecture: Principal Systems Engineer required to architect high-performance distributed state machines and manage low-level integration using memory-unmanaged or strictly typed languages such as C++, Rust, or Zig. Core focus is on performance primitives: asynchronous I/O, lock-free data structures, and cache-coherent algorithms. Deep knowledge of language internals, including garbage collection tuning, memory safety lifetimes, and compiler-level optimizations is mandatory. Candidates must handle complex concurrency primitives, debugging race conditions and distributed deadlocks in high-throughput environments where performance is measured in microseconds.  Infrastructure, Networking & Container Orchestration: Manage massive-scale container orchestration via Kubernetes, involving the development of custom CRDs and operators. Oversee service mesh architectures (Istio/Envoy) focusing on mTLS, circuit breaking, and complex traffic routing. Infrastructure is managed strictly through code (Terraform, Pulumi, HCL), ensuring 99.999% availability across multi-region VPC deployments. Deep dive into networking layers, handling BGP routing, load-balancing algorithms, and implementing eBPF-based observability for kernel-level performance monitoring. Knowledge of bare-metal hypervisors and hardware resource isolation is essential.  Distributed Data, Database Internals & State: Perform deep-dive PostgreSQL performance tuning, including Write-Ahead Log (WAL) analysis, index bloat management, and query plan optimization. Implement distributed consensus protocols (Raft, Paxos) for maintaining state across sharded database clusters. Design low-latency data pipelines requiring expert-level knowledge of partitioning, ACID compliance at scale, and custom binary serialization formats (Protobuf, Avro) for high-efficiency data transit. Focus on internal storage engine mechanics and physical data layout.  SRE, Security Hardening & Systems Observability: Execute rigorous Site Reliability Engineering (SRE) and Zero Trust security frameworks. Manage SOPS/KMS for secret management and CI/CD security hardening to prevent supply chain attacks. Daily tasks involve pprof profiling, assembly-level debugging, and kernel-level trace analysis to resolve production bottlenecks. This is a strictly technical, hands-on role focused on the mechanical sympathy between software and hardware. No business-facing project management or high-level strategic integration is involved; the focus is entirely on the foundational engineering plumbing.

Role: AI Implementation Architect & GTM Systems Lead
Core Objective
To architect the "Intelligent Context Layer" of the organization by bridging the gap between stakeholder strategic intent and autonomous execution. This role focuses on the Discovery, Orchestration, and Scaling of AI systems, transforming messy enterprise data (Salesforce, SQL) into a high-fidelity "Data Backbone" that powers noise-free agentic workflows.

Responsibilities & Systems Orchestration
Discovery & Data Strategy: Lead discovery workshops with stakeholders (Marketing, Sales, RevOps) to identify high-ROI AI opportunities. Translate abstract business cases into technical specifications, focusing on Salesforce/CRM data integrity, deduplication, and enrichment as the foundation for intelligence.

Context Layer Architecture: Design and maintain a centralized, real-time context retrieval system (The "GTM Brain"). Engineer versioned API endpoints that allow agents to access clean, enriched data with consistent response contracts and sub-second latency.

Workflow Orchestration: Design and deploy production-grade automation via n8n or similar visual platforms. Manage complex logic branches, webhooks, and state-sync architectures (Supabase/Postgres) to create a seamless flow between frontier LLMs and enterprise systems.

Enablement & Scaling: Create "Starter Patterns" and documented context templates to make AI infrastructure accessible to non-engineers. Ensure the system can scale from 10 to 200+ agents without data drift or technical debt, maintaining operational rigor through monitoring and observability.

Technical Requirements & Methodologies
AI-Assisted Development: Expert-level proficiency in leveraging LLMs to accelerate development—using AI for code generation, syntax debugging, and optimizing custom Python/JavaScript snippets to extend orchestration beyond standard nodes.

The Bridge Stack: Hands-on mastery of the "Orchestration Trinity": n8n, Supabase/Postgres, and Salesforce/API-first architectures. Expert understanding of RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) and prompt versioning.

Methodology: A "Product Thinking" approach to data—understanding not just the "how" but the "why" of data flow. Comfortable navigating the ambiguity of building "from the ground up" while ensuring backward compatibility and stability.

Sector Preference & Impact
Strategic Focus: Strong interest in high-scale Enterprise AI, GTM ecosystems, or Open Source development. Prioritizes projects that deliver measurable growth, transparency, and operational efficiency through "Boring Infrastructure"—reliable systems that run without disruption.

The Non-Technical Constraint
The Engine Room Ban: This role specifically avoids low-level kernel work, manual memory management (C++/Rust), and bare-metal infrastructure. The focus is Application-Level Intelligence and Business Logic Orchestration.
